Verifying KernelSU and the Shizuku connection.
Complete these in order before activating root.
Run before uptime reaches 180s. Higher kernel panic risk. Resets when the app closes.

The 180s wait lets the kernel finish post-boot settling. Running the exploit early increases the chance of a kernel panic and reboot. Only bypass if the device is idle and settled.\n\nThe one-attempt-per-boot rule still applies.
Settle gate bypassed: uptime is under 180s, panic risk is higher.
If KernelSU modules or LSPosed are not active, run these in order.
Reapplies KernelSU modules. Does not restart the device or the Android app runtime.
Restarts the Android app runtime so LSPosed can attach.
Technical info and run history. Not needed for normal use.

RAM-only method for SM-S948U AZF1 only. Requires an already-running and authorized Shizuku server. System partitions and Knox are not modified, and root is removed on reboot.\n\nThe device may reboot during the run, so save important work first. After success, per-app root permissions are managed in KernelSU.

Shizuku is required: start the Shizuku server via ADB and authorize this app, then retry. The unprivileged fallback is disabled on AZF1 after repeated scan timeouts and kernel panics. This boot\'s attempt was not consumed.

Reruns the late-load, mount, and service stages of all currently active KernelSU modules. Other modules run too, so disable any suspect module first.\n\nThis does not restart the kernel or the Android app runtime. Run ‘soft boot’ when done.

Finish ‘module reload’ first. LSPosed and Zygisk attach to the newly started Android app runtime (Zygote).\n\nRunning apps and System UI will briefly stop. On some devices this may turn into a full reboot, which removes temporary root.
KernelSU Manager is not installed, tap to install.
